title: When are two bracket expressions equal?
description: Three pairs of expressions that differ only in where the bracket sits are worked out and compared. The video shows when moving a bracket keeps the value the same.
teaching_notes: Let the child try first, then compare. One idea: moving a bracket after a minus sign changes the value unless the signs inside are flipped. Ask the child to guess before working out.

video_script.why: The child works out three pairs of expressions and decides when moving a bracket keeps the value the same, using the sign before the bracket.
video_script.substitution: The same check works with other numbers: work out both expressions of a pair and compare.
video_script.anchor: three pairs of expressions with brackets in different places
video_script.payoff_line: The pairs are equal when the signs inside the bracket are handled properly.

final_answer.value: (a) 14 and 14, equal (b) 11 and 5, not equal (c) 5 and 5, equal
final_answer.spoken: fourteen and fourteen, equal; eleven and five, not equal; five and five, equal

maths_rules: in the first pair the bracket only groups added terms; in the third the signs were flipped properly; in the second the bracket after the minus was moved without flipping
video_script.design: One idea: a bracket can move freely when it only groups added terms or when the signs inside are flipped properly. The three pairs stay in the anchor band; the working band shows the values side by side. No hard clear.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, in the first pair, sixteen minus two is fourteen.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>On the other side, ten minus two is eight, and six plus eight is fourteen.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The two values are equal.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, in the second pair, eight minus three is five, and sixteen minus five is eleven.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>On the other side, sixteen minus eight is eight, and eight minus three is five.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Eleven and five are not equal.

marks.m3: an equals sign joins the two values

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, in the third pair, eighteen plus four is twenty two.
Twenty seven minus twenty two is five.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>On the other side, minus eighteen minus four is minus twenty two.
Twenty seven plus that is also five.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Both values are five, so they are equal.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step four, when are the pairs equal?
In the first pair, the bracket only groups added terms.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>In the third pair, the signs inside were flipped properly.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>In the second pair, the bracket after the minus was moved without flipping the signs.
